clue.text: 16A old man's holding up map the wrong way round

definitions.note: 16A is PLAIN; pampas is a plural noun for the plains of South America

indicators.note: in a down entry, holding up means supporting from below, so this piece sits under the other
something the wrong way round faces backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written
pa is an informal word for father, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: An old man holds a map upside down while lost on open grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 16A refers to PLAIN. 'Holding' tempts you to put one piece inside the other, but in this down light PA'S sits below the reversed map, supporting it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast treeless grasslands of Argentina, a classic example of a plain.

clue.text: A famous 17, 17, 17 film with Sandra Bullock

parts.note: 17 is BOB; the comedian Bob Hope is a famous Bob
to bob is to float, and more than one bob gives the plural

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a well-known movie starring Sandra Bullock.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is the answer BOB, used first as a name (Bob Hope) and then as a verb meaning to float on water.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope Floats is a 1998 romantic drama in which Sandra Bullock played the lead role.

clue.text: Secretary left without the FT is livid

parts.note: PA stands for personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letters are dropped from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
the two letters to remove, as written

explanation.surface: An office secretary is furious that the Financial Times has not been delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT looks like the newspaper, but it is just the letters F and T taken out of LEFT. Livid has an older sense of ashen or pallid.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid can mean deathly white or leaden in colour, a synonym for having lost colour.

clue.text: What you 17 for is relevant, bar one

indicators.note: bar means except, so the following letter is left out

parts.note: something that applies is relevant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A comment that what you are searching for is pertinent, with one exception.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is BOB: bobbing for apples is a party game of catching floating apples with your teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game of bobbing, players try to grab fruit floating in a tub of water using only their mouths.

clue.text: New dustmen are not sorted by academic ability

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Newly hired refuse collectors have not been grouped by how clever they are.
explanation.walkthrough: Streaming is the British school practice of putting pupils into classes by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: An unstreamed class mixes pupils of all abilities instead of dividing them into ranked groups.

clue.text: Swap last pair then middle pair of 3, ringing changes

indicators.text: Swap last pair then middle pair
indicators.note: exchanging two adjacent letters, twice over, gives a precise rearrangement of the word

parts.note: the answer to 3 down

explanation.surface: Instructions for bell-ringers to swap the order of bells, as in change ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: PALE becomes PAEL when its last two letters swap, then PEAL when its middle two swap, mimicking how ringers swap adjacent bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a long series of changes rung on a set of church bells.

clue.text: Person using ticket in response to offer

parts.note: as in acting at someone's request
a tender is a formal offer

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a ticket because they were offered one.
explanation.definitionFit: An attender is someone present at an event, typically admitted by showing a ticket.

clue.text: Nose traveller follows back from India

indicators.note: coming after means this piece is placed second in the answer
the back of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
the Roma are a traditionally travelling people

explanation.surface: A traveller with a good nose comes back from a trip to India.
explanation.definitionFit: Nose is a wine-tasting term for the smell or bouquet of a drink.

clue.text: Relative starts to do elegant swan impression

indicators.note: starts are opening letters, so only the first of each word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of each word
a pen is a female swan
a dent is an impression in a surface

explanation.surface: Someone is told to start doing a graceful imitation of a swan.
explanation.walkthrough: Relative looks like a noun for a family member, but here it is the adjective, as in relative to.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relative to another thing is contingent on it, the adjectival sense of conditional.

clue.text: Secret internet — we'd be crazy keeping record

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other
something crazy is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone says going onto a hidden part of the internet would be mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep web is the part of the internet that search engines do not index, so it stays hidden.

clue.text: Pastry Lee Mack shortly demolished, bit by bit

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked apart, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt
made short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: The comedian Lee Mack wolfed down a pastry in little bites.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee Mack is a British comedian and TV panel-show regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually, one part at a time, rather than all together.

clue.text: Flat ceramic includes date mark in Spanish

indicators.note: to include is to take in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a tile is a flat piece of fired clay
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A flat ceramic piece bears a date stamp, written in Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the wavy accent over the N in Spanish words such as señor.

clue.text: Jump on ice that hurts after jarring clash

indicators.note: coming after means this piece is placed at the end
jarring means jolting, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
ow is what you cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: A skater's jump on the ice ends in a painful collision.
explanation.definitionFit: The salchow is a figure-skating jump, named after the Swedish skater Ulrich Salchow.

clue.text: Jointly take bananas to lost property?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: together, side by side
second meaning: to hand in a bunch of bananas, a cluster called a hand, at a lost-property office

explanation.walkthrough: A bunch of bananas is called a hand, and to take a found item to lost property is to hand it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand in hand means closely together, as partners act jointly in a shared venture.

clue.text: Staggered by 16A and D

parts.note: 16A is PLAIN, and a steppe is a vast plain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is left reeling by a flat landscape and a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered and stepped both describe things arranged in offset stages, like terraced rows.

clue.text: Miniature portrait of Victoria, 12 for a 17?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first postage stamp, printed with the young Queen's head
second meaning: 17 is BOB, slang for a shilling, and twelve old pennies made one

explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the British shilling, worth twelve pre-decimal pennies; the 12 here is a number, not a clue reference.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1840 Penny Black was the first adhesive postage stamp, bearing a profile of Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Design unfinished and home undecorated

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a plan is a design, here cut short
being home is being in

explanation.surface: An unfinished design leaves a house bare and unadorned.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means simple and without ornament, a synonym for unadorned.

clue.text: No trouble taking 50 away from 16A + 19

indicators.note: taking away means removing, so a Roman fifty is struck out

parts.note: the answer to 16 across
19 is MINOR, and minor means lesser

explanation.surface: A sum done without bother by subtracting fifty from two numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the Roman numeral for 50, taken out of PLAIN to leave PAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Painless can describe a task that causes no difficulty at all, an easy one.

clue.text: Builder who's 27 29 when the job's done

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the children's TV character who is a builder
second meaning: 27 and 29 are YOUR and UNCLE, completing the phrase said when something is sorted

explanation.walkthrough: Bob's your uncle is a British phrase meaning 'and there you are, done'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob the Builder is a cartoon tradesman, and the idiom names the same man as everyone's uncle.

clue.text: Decadent place has honey left over

parts.note: both are terms of endearment
L is the abbreviation for left
on means over or upon

explanation.surface: A den of vice still has some honey that nobody ate.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon, the ancient city, became a byword for luxury and moral corruption.

clue.text: Child pally with old Mr Banks

indicators.note: riverbanks lie either side of the water, so this piece flanks the other

parts.note: taken as written
being in with someone is being friendly with them
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A child gets friendly with old Mr Banks, the father in Mary Poppins.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Banks looks like a name, but 'banks' is the instruction for MR to surround the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is a person below the age of legal adulthood, a young person in law.

clue.text: Curving flight of e.g. fly cut in half — what keeps it up?

indicators.note: halving a word keeps only its front portion and drops the rest

parts.note: a fly is an example of a creepy-crawly
a wing is what keeps a flying thing in the air

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at how a halved fly could still fly in a curve.
explanation.walkthrough: Inswing is a cricket term: a bowled ball that curves in the air towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a delivery's swing is its sideways curve through the air, and inward swing moves toward the batter.

clue.text: Try British league and French cup

parts.note: to have a go is to try
B is the abbreviation for British
L is the abbreviation for league
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A football team chases success in the British league and a French cup competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French cup' looks like a single trophy, but French belongs with 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a drinking vessel with a stem and foot, a kind of cup.

clue.text: Barefooted South African agreed to make friends

parts.note: Zola Budd, the South African runner famous for racing barefoot
yup is an informal yes

explanation.surface: A shoeless South African says yes to becoming friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Zola Budd was a 1980s South African distance runner who ran without shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: To buddy up is to pair off with someone as a companion or partner.

clue.text: Quickly deflate favourite doll

parts.note: a balloon pops when it deflates suddenly
a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A child's best-loved inflatable doll goes down in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Doll and poppet are both affectionate terms for a sweet young person; a poppet was also once a small doll.

clue.text: Meal with different side for you to take out

indicators.note: a different side means a neighbouring key is used in place of one letter

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal
U is text-speak for you, the letter replaced

explanation.surface: A takeaway meal comes with a different side dish for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The U in LUNCH is swapped for Y, the key beside U on a keyboard, giving LYNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out is slang for killing someone, and to lynch is to kill by mob violence.

clue.text: Central section of Lexington Avenue

indicators.note: of means drawn from within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A description of the middle stretch of a New York street.
explanation.definitionFit: The nave is the main central body of a church where the congregation sits.

clue.text: Disastrous attempt at 16A 17 19 falling flat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Plain Bob Minor is a bell-ringing method
second meaning: a dive landing stomach-first on the water

explanation.walkthrough: 16A 17 19 reads PLAIN BOB MINOR, a standard method in English change ringing on six bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A belly flop is a clumsy dive that hits the water flat, and figuratively an embarrassing failure.

clue.text: A typical year, banking bonus regularly

indicators.note: banking means holding on deposit, so one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: YR is the abbreviation for year

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: An ordinary year in which a bonus gets paid into the bank every time.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'your average voter', this word can mean typical or ordinary, standing for an indefinite article plus 'typical'.

clue.text: Still 19, just one away from 18

parts.note: surface: a reference to the number nineteen; cryptically 19 is MINOR, so still under age
setter's reading: a year short of the age of adulthood

explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look arithmetic, but 19 is the answer MINOR: someone still a minor and one year short of turning 18.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighteen is the age of majority in Britain, so a person a year younger is the oldest kind of child.

clue.text: Parents' friend has name in cryptic clue

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
something cryptic is puzzling and scrambled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A family friend's name appears in a crossword clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Children often call a close male friend of their parents 'uncle' as an honorary title.
